Definition: from G1537 and G649; to send away forth, i.e. (on a mission) to despatch, or (peremptorily) to dismiss:--send (away, forth, out).
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, exapostéllō is the word for send (away, forth, out). In Mark 16:8, the text says "And they went out quickly." In Luke 1:53, the text says "and the rich he hath sent empty away."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that exapostéllō matters because the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
